arxiv-2205-05098.title: Graph-theoretic approach to Bell experiments with low detection efficiency
arxiv-2205-05098.creator: Zhen-Peng Xu, Jonathan Steinberg, Jaskaran Singh, Antonio J. López-Tarrida, José R. Portillo, Adán Cabello
arxiv-2205-05098.description: Abstract Bell inequality tests where the detection efficiency is below a certain threshold η crit \eta_{\rm{crit}} can be simulated with local hidden-variable models. Here, we introduce a method to identify Bell tests requiring low η crit \eta_{\rm{crit}} and relatively low dimension d d of the local quantum systems. The method has two steps.

arxiv-2310-11052.title: Investigating Threats Posed by SMS Origin Spoofing to IoT Devices Journal: DTRAP
arxiv-2310-11052.creator: Akaki Tsunoda
arxiv-2310-11052.description: Abstract . The short message service (SMS) is a service for exchanging texts via mobile networks that has been developed not only as a means of text communication between subscribers but also as a means to remotely manage Internet of Things (IoT) devices. However, the originating number of an SMS can be spoofed.

arxiv-2403-11954.title: Robust Estimation and Inference for Categorical Data Thanks: I thank Andreas Alfons, Isaiah Andrews, Patrick Groenen, Karen Kafadar, Patrick Mair, Anna Mikusheva, Whitney Newey, Mikhail Zhelonkin, as well as the participants of the MIT Econometrics lunch seminar and the Econometric Institute interna
arxiv-2403-11954.creator: Max Welz
arxiv-2403-11954.description: Abstract While there is a rich literature on robust methodologies for contamination in continuously distributed data, contamination in categorical data is largely overlooked. This is regrettable because many datasets are categorical and oftentimes suffer from contamination. Examples include inattentive responding and bot responses in questionnaires or zero-inflated count data.

arxiv-2504-17891.title: Do We Need Transformers to Play FPS Video Games?
arxiv-2504-17891.creator: Karmanbir Batth, Krish Sethi, Aly Shariff, Leo Shi, Hetul Patel
arxiv-2504-17891.description: Abstract In this paper, we explore the Transformer based architectures for reinforcement learning in both online and offline settings within the Doom game environment. Our investigation focuses on two primary approaches: Deep Transformer Q-learning Networks (DTQN) for online learning [ 1 ] and Decision Transformers (DT) for offline reinforcement learning [ 2 ] .

arxiv-2507-14383.title: Quantum Internet in a Nutshell – Advancing Quantum Communication with Ion Traps
arxiv-2507-14383.creator: Janine Hilder, Sascha Heußen, Anke Ginter, Andreas Wilke, Lukas Postler, Ulrich Poschinger, Ferdinand Schmidt-Kaler, Wadim Wormsbecher
arxiv-2507-14383.description: Abstract Quantum Internet in a Nutshell (QI-Nutshell) connects the fields of quantum communication and quantum computing by emulating quantum communication protocols on currently available ion-trap quantum computers. We demonstrate emulations of QKD protocols where the individual steps are mapped to physical operations within our hardware platform.

arxiv-2509-26595.title: Profit Maximization for a Robotics-as-a-Service Model
arxiv-2509-26595.creator: Joo Seung Lee, Anil Aswani
arxiv-2509-26595.description: Abstract The growth of Robotics-as-a-Service (RaaS) presents new operational challenges, particularly in optimizing business decisions like pricing and equipment management. While much research focuses on the technical aspects of RaaS, the strategic business problems of joint pricing and replacement have been less explored.

britannica-1911-hero-of-alexandria.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-hero-of-alexandria.description: Article 'Hero of Alexandria' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 13), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. mechanical and physical subjects, probably flourished in the second half of the 1st century. This is the more modern view, in contrast to the earlier theory most generally accepted, according to which he flourished about 100 B.C. The earlier theory started from the superscription of one of his works, Ἥρωνος Κτησιβίου βελοποιϊκά , from which it was inferred that Hero was a pupil of Ctesibius.

europmc-pmc5420141.title: Optimizing methods and dodging pitfalls in microbiome research.
europmc-pmc5420141.creator: Kim D, Hofstaedter CE, Zhao C, Mattei L, Tanes C, Clarke E, Lauder A, Sherrill-Mix S, Chehoud C, Kelsen J, Conrad M, Collman RG, Baldassano R, Bushman FD, Bittinger K.

pmc-10603952.title: Legend or Truth: Mature CD4+CD8+ Double-Positive T Cells in the Periphery in Health and Disease
pmc-10603952.creator: Magdalena Hagen, Luca Pangrazzi, Lourdes Rocamora-Reverte, Birgit Weinberger, Amedeo Amedei
pmc-10603952.description: The expression of CD4 and CD8 co-receptors defines two distinct T cell populations with specialized functions. While CD4+ T cells support and modulate immune responses through different T-helper (Th) and regulatory subtypes, CD8+ T cells eliminate cells that might threaten the organism, for example, virus-infected or tumor cells.

pmc-10737909.title: RISK FACTORS FOR FALL-RELATED MILD TRAUMATIC BRAIN INJURIES AMONG OLDER ADULTS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW
pmc-10737909.creator: Prince Okrah, Shafer Tharrington, Isaac Shin, Aaron Wagoner, Katelyn Woodsmall, Deborah Jehu
pmc-10737909.description: Mild traumatic brain injuries (mTBI) are commonly undiagnosed, which delays treatment and recovery. About 80% of older adults’ mTBIs stem from falls, yet factors driving fall-related mTBIs are unclear. This study aimed to systematically review risk factors for fall-related mTBIs among older adults.

pmc-11359001.title: Effects of Shading Nets Color on the Internal Environmental Conditions, Light Spectral Distribution, and Strawberry Growth and Yield in Greenhouses
pmc-11359001.creator: Ibrahim M. Alhelal, Ammar A. Albadawi, Abdullah A. Alsadon, Mekhled M. Alenazi, Abdullah A. Ibrahim, Mohamed Shady, Abdulhakim A. Al-Dubai
pmc-11359001.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Greenhouses are used to create the appropriate environment for plant growth. Controlling the level of lighting using shading nets is one of the most commonly used methods for making suitable environmental modifications in greenhouses.

pmc-11535184.title: GLCCI1 alleviates GRP78-initiated endoplasmic reticulum stress-induced apoptosis of retinal ganglion cells in diabetic retinopathy by upregulating and interacting with HSP90AB1
pmc-11535184.creator: Jiayou Liu, Hongdan Yu, Shengxue Yu, Mengren Liu, Xinyuan Chen, Yufei Wang, Jing Li, Caixing Shi, Wenqiang Liu, Zhongfu Zuo, Xuezheng Liu
pmc-11535184.description: Retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) are among the first neurons to undergo apoptosis in diabetic retinopathy (DR), with their relationship to endoplasmic reticulum stress (ERS)-induced apoptosis still unclear. While glucocorticoid-induced transcript 1 (GLCCI1) has been shown to inhibit apoptosis, its role in ERS-induced apoptosis and its mechanisms in DR remain unclarified.

pmc-11633709.title: Evaluating depression in Indonesian adolescents with epilepsy: Comprehensive validation and reliability assessment of the neurological disorders depression inventory‐epilepsy for youth Indonesian version (NDDI‐E‐Y[ID])
pmc-11633709.creator: Setyo Handryastuti, Tjhin Wiguna, Novie Amelia Chozie, Bernie Endyarni Medise, Wahyuni Indawati, Cut Nurul Hafifah, Widdy Winarta
pmc-11633709.description: ObjectivesEpilepsy is a common chronic neurological disorder in pediatrics. Depression is an often underdetected comorbidity in childhood epilepsy. This study aimed to adapt the Neurological Disorders Depression Inventory‐Epilepsy for Youth (NDDI‐E‐Y) to the Indonesian language and population, as well as to validate the Indonesian version of NDDI‐E‐Y (NDDI‐E‐Y[ID]).

pmc-12451528.title: Metal–organic frameworks for biomedical applications: bridging materials science and regenerative medicine
pmc-12451528.creator: Negar Nasri, Marziyeh Azad, Zahra Mehrabi, Ghasem Dini, Afsaneh Marandi
pmc-12451528.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). This review explores the biomedical applications of metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), focusing on their potential in bone regeneration. Due to their high porosity, tunable structures, and biocompatibility, MOFs have emerged as promising candidates for bone tissue engineering. This article discusses the synthesis and functionalization of MOFs at the micro- and nanoscale, their interactions with biological environments, and their roles in drug delivery, osteoinduction, and osteoconduction. Recent advancements in theranostic MOF-based scaffolds, which integrate both therapeutic and diagnostic functions, are also highlighted.

pmc-12504662.title: Hydrogen sulfide pretreatment mitigates the adverse effects of salinity in young carob seedlings
pmc-12504662.creator: Saeid Eshghi, Farzad Amiri Bahmanbiglo, Sahar Mirzaei, Babak Jamali, Iman Mirmazloum, David Papp
pmc-12504662.description: Despite the inherent high salinity tolerance of mature carob (Ceratonia siliqua L., Fabaceae) trees, young seedlings are particularly vulnerable to salt stress, which can hinder their growth and development. Although hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) has been widely studied as a regulator of salinity tolerance in herbaceous plants, its role in woody legumes remains largely unexplored.

pmc-12514568.title: Metabolic syndrome in perimenopausal and postmenopausal women attending gynaecology outpatient department at a tertiary institution in South Africa
pmc-12514568.creator: Lawrence Marapo, Lineo Matsela, ME Chabalala, Olakunle Adewunmi Towobola
pmc-12514568.description: BackgroundThe prevalence of metabolic syndrome in menopause varies globally. There is a paucity of data regarding knowledge of metabolic syndrome in menopause in South Africa.Objective(s)The study was designed to describe the prevalence of metabolic syndrome in perimenopausal and postmenopausal and the lipid changes that occur during the menopause transition.

pmc-12568127.title: Neutralisation of the Immunoglobulin-Cleaving Activity of Streptococcus equi Subspecies equi IdeE by Blood Sera from Ponies Vaccinated with a Multicomponent Protein Vaccine
pmc-12568127.creator: Francesco Righetti, Karina Hentrich, Margareta Flock, Sara Frosth, Karin Jacobsson, Joakim Bjerketorp, Anuj Pathak, Noela Ido, Birgitta Henriques-Normark, Lars Frykberg, Romain Paillot, Bengt Guss, Tim Wood, Jan-Ingmar Flock, Andrew Stephen Waller, José M Rojas, Verónica Martín, Noemí Sevilla
pmc-12568127.description: Background: Streptococcus equi subspecies equi (S. equi) is the cause of strangles, one of the most prevalent diseases of horses worldwide. The disease is characterised by fever and the formation of abscesses in the lymph nodes of the head and neck, which can restrict the airway.

pmc-12655391.title: Nanostructured Delivery Systems for Curcumin: Improving Bioavailability and Plaque-Targeting Efficacy in Atherosclerosis
pmc-12655391.creator: Yu Liu, Tengfei Yu, Chao Zhang, Zhiyong Yang, Dahai Yu, Bin He, Yan Liang, Fátima Regina Mena Barreto Silva, Diana Marcela Aragon Novoa
pmc-12655391.description: Cardiovascular disease (CVD) encompasses ischemic conditions of the heart, brain, and bodily tissues, primarily resulting from hyperlipidemia, atherosclerosis (AS), hypertension, and other related factors. CVD accounts for over 40% of global non-communicable disease mortality, making it the leading cause of death and a significant medical burden worldwide.

pmc-12739945.title: Investigating Self-Reported Sensory Intolerance and Perceptual Ability Across Sensory Modalities in Fibromyalgia
pmc-12739945.creator: Hayley Shepherd, Ellen Poliakoff, Christopher A Brown, Richard J Brown
pmc-12739945.description: PurposeFibromyalgia has predominantly been classified as a condition of amplified pain processing associated with greater sensitivity to pain. Beyond disturbed pain processing, emerging evidence suggests that people with fibromyalgia experience intolerances (increased unpleasantness) across sensory modalities. Limited research, however, has investigated how discrimination and detection in different senses are affected in this group.

pmc-12740956.title: Dual learning systems in talker identification: the effects of language, accent, and feedback
pmc-12740956.creator: Shengyue Xiong, Zhe-chen Guo, Casey L Roark, Gangyi Feng, Bharath Chandrasekaran
pmc-12740956.description: Talker identification categorizes variable speech signals into stable talker representations, a process facilitated by language and accent familiarity. The dual learning systems (DLS) model posits that speech category learning involves a “reflective” system based on explicit rules and a “reflexive” system based on stimulus-reward associations, with reflexive learning dominating in later stages.

pmc-12817805.title: Is Bariatric Surgery at Risk Due to Semaglutide?
pmc-12817805.creator: Jane Tian, Shubham Bhatia, Christina Sneed, Patrick Kiarie, Mikayla Fuchs, Andrew Miele, Darshak Shah, Noman Khan, Martine A. Louis
pmc-12817805.description: PurposeObesity remains a significant public health issue in the Western world, affecting millions of Americans and contributing to chronic conditions such as diabetes and hypertension. In June 2021, the Food and Drug Administration approved semaglutide for long-term weight management. While its effectiveness in promoting weight loss has been well-documented, its impact on the field of bariatric surgery remains uncertain.

pmc-13386797.title: AI-based fundus screening of teachers: fundus tessellated density as a myopia biomarker and occupational associations
pmc-13386797.creator: Zhongnan Xiao, Huijuan Liu, Hongyan Wang, Min Song, Guoquan Liu, Chunhong Yin, Liwei Liu, Min Li, Jingmiao Sun, Yi Ren, Ying Guo, Yu Zhong, Hong Yu, Ying Liu
pmc-13386797.description: BackgroundArtificial intelligence (AI)-based fundus imaging enables efficient large-scale retinal screening; however, its application in occupational populations remains limited.ObjectiveTo evaluate the utility of an AI-based fundus screening system in teachers and to investigate fundus tessellated density (FTD) as a potential imaging marker associated with myopia and occupational factors.

pmc-13688756.title: Economic burden of road traffic injuries in Iran; time to make tough decisions: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13688756.creator: Habib Omranikhoo, Anahita Nicknam, Hedaiat Salari, Mahbobeh Shahbazifard, Mehdi Rezaee
pmc-13688756.description: ObjectivesRoad traffic injuries (RTIs) constitute a serious challenge for human societies, imposing a substantial economic burden on countries and representing the leading cause of death among children and youth between the ages of 5 and 29. Estimates indicate that RTIs are on track to become the fifth leading cause of death globally by 2030.
